title: Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading (Eliseev, Mazur; arXiv 2312.17238v1, 28 Dec 2023)
setup: Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (46.7B, 8 experts/layer, top-2), HQQ attn 4-bit + experts 2/3-bit; T4 16GB, RTX 3060 12GB, RTX 3080 Mobile 16GB, A100 reference; PCIe, host RAM (no SSD); batch 1, sampling, OpenAssistant; per-layer LRU k=2 (12GB) or k=4 (16GB); speculative loading of 1-2 experts via next layer gate on current hidden state; baseline accelerate naive offloading

numbers.what: full vs no LRU and no preload
LRU only gain (without preload / without both)
MMLU 5-shot FP16 vs 4b attn + 2b experts vs 3b experts

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: Offloading suits large batches; interactive much slower
catalog_numbers_correct.correct: yes (paraphrase of Sec 2.3 motivation about prior work; no number; not a result of this paper)

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: first pass: LRU+preload 1.4-1.8x over no cache

why: LRU reuse and batch-1 argument transfer; breaks: GPU compute and PCIe from host RAM not SSD, cache is 25-50% of experts per layer vs 4-20 token footprints of 24,576 experts for us, top-2/8 vs top-10/512, 2-bit quant; speculative-load gain needs evaluation at 512 experts
quality_loss: LRU and speculation lossless; quantization only: MMLU 70.51 -> 65.58 (2-bit experts) or 68.47 (3-bit experts); Wiki2 3.59 -> 4.61/4.05
ablation: Table 2 isolates LRU, preload, naive; no layout ablation
limitations: No explicit limitation section; exact next-layer prefetch impossible without retraining (Sec 3.2); future work only
contradicts_our_findings: No. Note per-layer LRU with k=2 equals one token's top-2, so its LRU gain is within-layer reuse, not comparable to global LRU below one footprint (our 0.0 hit).

title: The Other Half of the Memory Wall: Serving 35B MoEs from SSD with Trained Routing Prediction (Edge0; Lin, Wang, Cai, Liu, Zeng; AutoArk; arXiv 2609.18063v2, 17 Sep 2026)
setup: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (40 layers x 256 experts, native top-8, 19.5GB int4 g64, 1.77MB/expert) narrowed to K=4 with recovery LoRA r=16 and 33 prerouter heads; 8B tier Ling 3.0 tiny 24x128 K=8; MLX only; Mac mini M4 Pro 24GB (tier table), MacBook M2 16GB (prerouter A/B, 18.4GiB checkpoint does not fit); mmap + OS page cache + LRU bundles; batch 1; storage bandwidth not stated; medians of 3 same-session rotated rounds, +-40% single-shot spread

B.md: naive on-demand streaming ineffective, 20.4 vs 3.9
catalog_numbers_correct.correct: no (3.9 is a fully resident engine; on-demand streaming without prerouter is 19.9)

why: Overlap-by-prediction idea and the findings (adjacent-token agreement ~25%, one-layer-ahead prediction loses to LRU) transfer; headline does not: Apple GPU/MLX, model nearly fits RAM (19.5GB in 16-24GB) vs ours 69GB in 8-32GB, retraining + LoRA required, K narrowed 8->4, disk read at most 12% of step, CPU graph building is the floor, gain shrinks on hot caches/fast storage
quality_loss: avg -4.0 points vs fp16 on 5 benchmarks (AIME -6.1 worst); 8B tier avg -2.8 (AIME -10.0); int4 + routing replacement not separated

contradicts_our_findings: B.md misdescribes it as showing naive streaming ineffective; the paper shows 19.9 tok/s streaming without the prerouter on 24GB.
